cluster_summary: This cluster covers vulnerabilities where user-controlled data is embedded into HTML, attributes, JavaScript, or CSS contexts without proper context-aware escaping, leading to cross-site scripting. The root causes include incomplete HTML entity encoding, missing script-context escaping for JSON, confusion between text and HTML sinks, and lack of dedicated escaping for different contexts.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled markup, HTML fragments, rich text, comments, DOM nodes, style blocks, attributes, or URI values into HTML cleaners, SafeHtml validators, DOM sanitizers, rich-text renderers, or browser-rendered sanitized output. Report code paths where the active sanitizer policy does not allowlist dangerous elements, attributes, URI schemes, DOM child nodes, comments, or malformed inputs before rendering. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 4 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should activate the restrictive sanitizer for the relevant mode, enforce element/attribute/URI allowlists after parsing, and add regression tests for the bypass form.

mechanism.missing_guard: the active sanitizer policy does not allowlist dangerous elements, attributes, URI schemes, DOM child nodes, comments, or malformed inputs before rendering
mechanism.name: HTML sanitizer policy gap or inactive allowlist
mechanism.sink_shape: HTML cleaners, SafeHtml validators, DOM sanitizers, rich-text renderers, or browser-rendered sanitized output
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-controlled markup, HTML fragments, rich text, comments, DOM nodes, style blocks, attributes, or URI values
mechanism.typical_fix: activate the restrictive sanitizer for the relevant mode, enforce element/attribute/URI allowlists after parsing, and add regression tests for the bypass form

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add missing escape cases for attribute-specific characters or apply full HTML entity encoding (e.g., escape & < > ' " ) to all string values before HTML insertion.
sub_patterns.name: Incomplete HTML entity escaping for attribute and general HTML contexts
sub_patterns.root_cause: The HTML escaper omitted characters that are special in attribute values (single quote, equals, backtick) or HTML entity encoding was entirely missing for JSON string values inserted into HTML.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Replace raw HTML insertion with text-safe methods such as document.createTextNode() or auto-escaped text interpolation, ensuring the data is treated as text rather than HTML.
sub_patterns.name: Inappropriate use of raw HTML sink for plain text data
sub_patterns.root_cause: The code assumed that user-controlled data (e.g., SSID, entity names) is safe to assign to innerHTML or render via @html, treating text as raw HTML without any escaping or sanitization.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add conditional escaping: output raw HTML only for innerHTML binding; apply HTML entity escaping for innerText, textContent, and similar text bindings.
sub_patterns.name: Missing context-sensitive escaping for contenteditable SSR bindings
sub_patterns.root_cause: Server-side rendering code treated all contenteditable bindings uniformly as innerHTML, failing to apply HTML escaping for innerText and textContent bindings which represent plain text.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add dedicated escaping functions for each context (HTML, attribute, JavaScript string, CSS color) and apply them at all interpolation points; for CSS colors, validate against a strict pattern and fallback to a safe default.
sub_patterns.name: Missing multi-context output encoding for HTML, attribute, JavaScript, and CSS
sub_patterns.root_cause: The code assumed that stored metadata (tag names, collection names) is safe for direct interpolation into HTML, HTML attributes, JavaScript template literals, and CSS style values without any context-appropriate escaping.
